column1: # ROW OWNERS — side table keyed on row id. MACHINE FILE, read by whose_row.py.
# WHY A SIDE TABLE AND NOT A COLUMN. `CLAIMS.md`'s twelve rows are up to ~1,800 characters
# (CLM-006); adding an owner column means rewriting every one of them, and a rewritten long
# line is the one thing git cannot merge. A side table is a pure addition: zero row edits,
# no freeze window, and it works identically for VALIDATION_LEDGER.md's 108 VL ids when
# someone is ready to fill those in.
# WHY OWNERS ARE NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE ID. BEN-* ids come in per-lane blocks, so a block
# table attributes them. CLM ids are SUBJECT-ALLOCATED — CLM-001 through CLM-012 were
# assigned in the order claims arose, by whichever lane was looking at that physics — so no
# arithmetic on the number yields a lane. Same for VL, which is written in arrival order by
# whichever lane measured the number. That is why this file exists and why it is hand-filled.
# `UNASSIGNED` IS NOT PERMISSION, AND THE GATE ENFORCES THAT.
# An id listed here with owner UNASSIGNED means "nobody has decided who owns this yet". It
# does NOT mean "any lane may edit it". `whose_row.py` exits 2 (CANNOT CHECK) on it, never 0.
# This is the same asymmetry that fixed the vacuous-pass family: a gate that examined a row
# and found no decision has NOT verified anything, and must not answer with the same exit
# code it uses for "verified yours".
# The twelve CLM assignments are deliberately left UNASSIGNED by Session A. Session A is the
# orchestrator; routing is its job and adjudicating physics ownership is not. Filling these
# in by judgement is precisely the error A instructed Session C against on the quoted set —
# derive the set from the artifacts, do not decide it.
# HOW THE `basis` COLUMN WAS ACTUALLY PRODUCED, corrected 2026-08-18 (quorum: lanes A, C, and
# the mediator). This header previously said each row was routed "to the lane that authored or
# verified the claim, per the row's own `independent verifier` field". THAT DERIVATION CANNOT
# HAVE BEEN PERFORMED. The field exists -- column 8 of CLAIMS.md's table, so the citation
# resolves -- but ZERO of the twelve name a lane. They name tools and sessions: "codex V1 +
# claude-school V2 (independent)", "agy (separate provider account, effort high)",
# "fresh-context claude-school opus x3", "single-source (this session)". A CITATION THAT
# RESOLVES IS NOT A CITATION THAT HOLDS.
# So the `basis` column is SUBJECT-MATTER JUDGEMENT, RECORDED FOR REVIEW -- not an artifact
# derivation, and not an assignment. It is a reading offered so a future adjudication starts
# somewhere, and it is explicitly NOT an answer to the ownership question.
# THE OWNER COLUMN MUST NOT BE BACK-FILLED FROM `basis`. Doing so would make the provenance
# CIRCULAR AND PASSING: the owner cell would cite `basis`, `basis` is judgement, and the header
# would then describe a derivation that both resolves AND supports the cell it feeds. Today the
# inconsistency is visible, which is what makes it fixable. The twelve stay UNASSIGNED until
# someone RULES them.
# The abstention itself is correct and is deliberately preserved: adjudicating physics ownership
# is not the orchestrator's job, and a raiser is not an owner.
# Each row's named lane fills its own line once ownership is ruled. See CONVENTION-lane-worktrees.md's author-merges-own-row rule.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated):
#   id        the row id exactly as it appears in the source file's leading cell
#   owner     a lane key matching FINDINGS.md's block table ("A", "B", "C", "D"), or
#             UNASSIGNED. Free text after the lane letter is allowed and ignored.
#   source    the file the id lives in; checked, so a typo'd id cannot sit here unnoticed
#   basis     WHY this lane, in a few words. A bare assignment with no basis is a guess
#             that has stopped looking like one.
